title: He Who Calls You Is Faithful
summary: Life brings mountaintops and valleys, and God calls us to rejoice always and give thanks in everything. We can't do that in our own power, but he is faithful.
exhortation: There is no better news to start our day than that we have been brought from death to life through the death and resurrection of Jesus. Jesus' death on our behalf is what we proclaim over and over again.

And even though that is the best news, we still live in a fallen world. Paul knows that, so he encourages the church in Thessalonica: "admonish the idle, encourage the fainthearted, help the weak, be patient with them all... Do not quench the Spirit... test everything; hold fast what is good. Abstain from every form of evil." And then: "Now may the God of peace himself sanctify you completely, and may your whole spirit and soul and body be kept blameless at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ."

I'm thankful he ends this way: "He who calls you is faithful; he will surely do it." The circumstances of life are all over the place. We experience joys and the deepest sorrows, mountaintops and valleys. And yet the Lord calls us to rejoice always, pray without ceasing and give thanks in all circumstances. He knows we can't do that in our own power, and for that I'm grateful. The Lord is faithful. He is the one who calls us, and he is faithful to help us in every season. He is the one who can make us say, "We are thankful."
prayer: Lord, give us hearts overwhelmed with gratitude at such a marvelous work. We pray against any creeping legalism that tries to find worth in ourselves, so that we simply say, "Thank you, Jesus," for such wondrous grace, abounding mercy and mercies new every morning.

Let all you have done flavor every part of our day. Bring to mind again and again: I am saved. I am redeemed. The sin Satan keeps trying to condemn me with is forgiven. I am a child of God, raised with him because I was buried with him. Fill us with thankfulness, Lord. Jesus, we are grateful.
